newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says no new taxes due to Senate move.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says no new taxes due to Senate move.

text.p: Australian treasurer Peter Costello said on Thursday that the government would not introduce new taxation measures due to the problems it was having in the upper house with the passage of revenue-based budget legislation.
"No new tax and we are not going to put up tax, there is no question of that," Costello said in a radio interview.
Costello said on Wednesday that the government would face a A$400 million shortfall over four years due to amendments to budget legislation in the Senate earlier this week.
The government does not have a majority in the Senate, which is the upper house of the Australian parliament.
The bill was the first major element of the government's deficit-slashing budget to come before the Senate.
The Senate is scheduled over the next two weeks to deal with most other bills in the budget programme, which aimed to save A$7.2 billion in the fiscal year to June 1998.
